title: Reframe routing decision runtime and consolidate regional state interfaces
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Over time the smart routing layer accumulated multiple ad-hoc state hand-offs: regional affinity caches, a legacy fallback queue, and several tiny policy adapters that each serialize different parts of the decision context. This has increased mutex contention, made debugging fallbacks painful, and slowed rollout of new policy rules.

Goal: Reframe the routing decision runtime by introducing a compact, read-optimized regional state interface and migrating the fallback logic into a single small state machine. The work should:
- Remove the global routing mutex and replace it with shard-local lock-free readers where possible.
- Consolidate regional affinity and admission state behind a single accessor API (RegionState) with clear read/write contracts.
- Replace the legacy fallback queue with an evented fallback state machine that emits transition events for tracing and metrics.
- Keep the public policy evaluation contract stable (no changes to API surface for callers).

Scope:
- Implement RegionState interface and adapters for current in-memory store and Redis-backed persistence.
- Build FallbackStateMachine with deterministic transitions and unit tests covering all existing fallback paths.
- Migrate two high-traffic policy adapters to the new interface as a proof-of-concept.
- Add end-to-end integration tests and synthetic load benchmarks to validate perf targets.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end p95 latency on routing decision path is not regressed; p99 should improve by at least 5% on replicated load tests.
- Global routing lock removed from hot path; contention metrics drop by 70% in staging.
- Fallbacks produce structured transition traces (trace ids present in logs) and corresponding UI events wired to Console.
- No behavioral changes for existing rollout policies when running behind the migration toggle.

Migration strategy:
1) Deploy RegionState adapter in parallel (feature flag) and run read-through mode.
2) Enable FallbackStateMachine behind a toggle for non-critical routes.
3) Gradually migrate policy adapters, monitor metrics/dashboards, rollback on anomalies.

Rollback: toggle off fallback state machine and revert to legacy queue adapter; RegionState supports both modes until fully drained.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: subtle policy ordering changes. Mitigation: add deterministic replay harness and run existing prompt-level integration tests.
- Risk: redis adapter introduces tail latency. Mitigation: add local cache layer + circuit-breaker for cold reads.

Perf targets: p50 ~ equal, p95 <= baseline, p99 -8% improvement, CPU utilization -10% on routing service under typical load.

Notes: This ticket focuses strictly on runtime/state consolidation and small adapter migrations. Larger reworks of policy DSL or rollout semantics are out-of-scope and will be separate tickets.
